suite_note: Both generations are measured with the same discovery command in the same clean-runtime shape. G1 adds tests to that suite, so the suite is not held constant in size; the honest comparison is capability added, not a score on a fixed holdout.

evaluator_held_novel_cases.reason: A holdout set written by an independent evaluator does not exist. Every test in this repository was written by the same producer that wrote the code under test, so no test here can serve as an evaluator-held novel case.

G0.commit_role: branch point of this Wave; the tree as seeded before Wave A

G1.label: Wave A transactional factory controls
G1.commit_note: The G1 commit is the head of cursor/po03-wave-a-transactional-factory-5086 after the final Wave A commit. It cannot be embedded in a file that is part of that commit; it is reported in the Wave return and recoverable with `git rev-parse`. Commits d67598a through the head are all G1.
G1.tests_total_note: The final suite count is recorded in receipts/po03/2026-08-22/producer-execution.json from the real final run, so this file cannot drift from it.
controls_added: changed-path allowlist guard enforced in CI for pull_request and push events, with rename detection disabled so a rename out of the allowlist cannot hide a deletion
content manifest over the tracked subtree with a CI verify gate, refusing symlinks and gitlinks
read-only repository disposition compilation with a partition guarantee and an alias cross-check against the taxonomy gate
directory-level validation of custody documents with fail-closed behaviour on an empty directory
per-unit transactional result documents with real artifact hashes and byte counts
operating-system metric definitions and one row per counted unit
anti-fabrication tests asserting every recorded commit id resolves to a real commit and every frozen source hash matches the branch-point bytes

G2.reason: No successor has been compiled from G1 field failures yet. G1 has not run live long enough to generate failures to learn from: its CI gates have not executed a single time on GitHub at the moment of recording, because the branch has not been pushed. Compiling a G2 now would mean inventing lessons rather than learning them.
G2.prerequisite: At least one real CI run of G1, plus an independent acceptance decision, so that G2 is compiled from observed failures rather than from anticipation.

claimed_lift.capability_delta_observed: G0 had no changed-path, manifest, disposition or directory-validation control. G1 has all four, each with executable tests and CI enforcement. That is an observable capability difference and it is not a measured lift.
claimed_lift.why_not_lift: Lift requires the same preregistered metric measured on both generations against a common holdout with no quality regression. The added tests are not a holdout: they were written alongside the code they exercise, so counting them as a score would measure test-writing volume rather than capability. No independent evaluator set exists, and no throughput or acceptance metric has a G0 baseline because G0 was never run as a factory.
claimed_lift.quality_regression_check: The 23 G0 invariant tests were re-run in isolation against G1 and all pass, so G1 does not regress any G0 invariant.
claimed_lift.three_generation_test_reason: The commission requires three measured generations. Two exist. G2 is deliberately withheld rather than fabricated.

lessons_that_changed_live_mechanisms.lesson: A changed-path base must be resolved against the wave's own base branch, not the default branch, or the guard fails on commits the wave never authored.
lessons_that_changed_live_mechanisms.recurrence_test: workstreams/po03/tests/test_path_scope_guard.py::CliTests and local execution of all four resolution branches

lessons_that_changed_live_mechanisms.lesson: Rename detection in git diff can hide a deletion outside the allowlist by reporting only the destination path.
lessons_that_changed_live_mechanisms.mechanism_change: --no-renames added to both diff invocations in the workflow

lessons_that_changed_live_mechanisms.lesson: A content manifest that follows symlinks can hash bytes from outside the subtree it claims to describe.
lessons_that_changed_live_mechanisms.mechanism_change: manifest.py enumerates git modes and refuses modes 120000 and 160000; manifest_text refuses symlinks directly

independent_recurrence_testing.reason: The three recurrence tests were written by the same producer that made the repairs. Independent recurrence testing requires a reviewer who did not write the fix.
